chunks: From him, from Muhammad ibn al-Hamid, from Sa'd ibn Zayd, who said:

Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) said: When you have prayed the Maghrib prayer, do not extend your leg and do not speak to anyone until you say one hundred times: 'Bismillah al-Rahman al-Rahim, La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'Ali al-'Azeem', and one hundred times in the morning. Whoever says it, Allah will repel from him one hundred types of afflictions; the least of which is vitiligo, leprosy, Satan, and the ruling authority.

key_terms.لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّه: There is no power and no strength except with Allah (a key dhikr phrase)

ai.seo_question: What is the recommended dhikr and etiquette after the Maghrib prayer to repel afflictions?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) prescribes reciting 'La hawla wa la quwwata illa billah al-'Ali al-'Azeem' one hundred times after Maghrib and in the morning to ward off diverse afflictions, ranging from physical ailments like leprosy to spiritual and social oppressions. This practice emphasizes a state of contemplative silence immediately following prayer, reflecting the Shia tradition of linking ritual purity with spiritual protection against both internal and external trials.

en.hubeali: From him, from Muhammad Bin Abdul Hameed, from Sa’ad Bin Zayd who said,

‘Abu Al-Hassanasws said: ‘Whenever you pray Al-Maghrib Salāt, so do not extend your legs and do not speak to anyone until you say ten times, ‘In the Name of Allahazwj the Beneficent, the Merciful. There is neither Might nor Strength except with Allahazwj, the Exalted, the Magnificent’, and one hundred times during the morning (Salat). So the one who says it, Allahazwj would Repel from him, one hundred types from the types of afflictions, the least from it being the vitiligo, and the leprosy, and the Satanla, and the ruling authority’.
en.sarwar: 29. It is narrated from him (narrator of the Hadith above) from Muhammad ibn ‘Abd al-Hamid from Sa’D ibn Zayd who has said the following:

“Abu al-Hassan (a.s.) has said, ‘When you performed your Maghrib prayer before stretching your leg or speaking to anyone say one hundred times, “(I begin) in the name of Allah, the Beneficent, the Merciful. There are no means and no power without Allah, the Most High, the Most Great,” and one hundred times in the morning, Allah will repel one hundred kinds of misfortune, the least of which is leprosy, Satan and rulers (unjust ones).”’
